analysis:
Examined both documentation excerpts, CLI metadata and all CLI patch hunks. Changes document add-on hold commands, a local socket/runtime directory, process-bound operator mailbox, bounded draining, model unloading, lease renewal and release, including an explicit force-release memory-contention warning. No executable controls are supplied in this batch; no concrete regression is established by these documentation changes. Unchanged surrounding cache, authorization, release, billing-related qualification and diagnostic guidance does not establish implementation behavior.
The new local availability-control surface intersects TB-003, TB-007 and TB-002; reconnect and release must preserve A-016 authorization and T-053 invalidation rules. docs/developer/test.md:768-790 describes permission, peer rejection, restart, lock/lease and reconnect tests, but expressly says positive signed-peer authentication is substituted in socket/serve-loop tests (788-790). CLI additions at docs/provider/cli-reference.md:156 and 1758 expose the command and runtime files; owner-only permissions alone do not authenticate an adversarial same-user operator.
Integration should inspect AddonCommand.swift, AddonHoldPaths.swift, ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift and the IPC peer/server implementations for authenticated peer identity, bounded connections/requests, safe file handling, mailbox process binding, drain/stop precedence, lock-versus-lease recovery and admission reopening only with current authorization. Determine whether the threat model needs a dedicated add-on IPC/VM resource-ownership boundary. Positive signed add-on interoperation remains explicitly unqualified; supplied documentation cannot resolve that contract. No change to encryption, cache tenant scoping (T-041), content telemetry or payment accounting is evidenced here.
